# Anvil - Complete .NET & Akka.NET Conventions Reference

> Opinionated .NET & Akka.NET conventions - forged from real projects.
> Source: https://anvil.st0o0.net

---

# Getting Started

---

## Project Scaffolding

Every new project starts from one of the template repositories. They include the root-level files, CI workflows, and tooling described below - so you get a working setup without manual assembly.

## Template repositories

| Template | Use for | Create |
|----------|---------|--------|
| [dotnet.application](https://github.com/st0o0/dotnet.application) | Services, APIs, Akka.NET apps with Docker | "Use this template" on GitHub |
| [dotnet.library](https://github.com/st0o0/dotnet.library) | NuGet packages | "Use this template" on GitHub |

Both are GitHub template repositories. Click "Use this template" to create a new repo with the full structure, then rename `ProjectName` to your actual project name.

:::tip
Always start from a template. Do not create a new repo from scratch and copy files over - the templates carry CI, release automation, commit linting, and security scanning that are easy to miss.
:::

## What the templates include

### Root-level files

```text
repo/
  global.json
  .editorconfig
  .config/
    dotnet-tools.json
  commitlint.config.mjs
  renovate.json
  release-please-config.json
  .release-please-manifest.json
  trivy.yaml
  src/
    ProjectName.slnx
    Directory.Build.props
    Directory.Packages.props
```

### CI and automation (pre-configured)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `commitlint.config.mjs` | Enforces [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, etc.) |
| `release-please-config.json` | Automatic versioning and changelog from commit messages |
| `renovate.json` | Automated dependency updates via Renovate |
| `trivy.yaml` | Container and dependency vulnerability scanning |

The CI workflows call reusable workflows from [github-workflows](https://github.com/st0o0/github-workflows). See [GitHub Actions](../ci/github-actions) for details.

## Solution format: .slnx

Use the `.slnx` XML solution format. It is human-readable, diff-friendly, and avoids the GUID noise of `.sln`.

```xml
<Solution>
  <Folder Name="/src/">
    <Project Path="ProjectName/ProjectName.csproj" />
    <Project Path="ProjectName.Core/ProjectName.Core.csproj" />
  </Folder>
</Solution>
```

## Directory.Build.props

Shared properties for every project in the tree.

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

## Central Package Management

Versions live in `Directory.Packages.props`. Project files reference packages without versions.

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageVersion Include="Akka" Version="1.5.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.v3" Version="1.0.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

:::tip
Use `dotnet add package` / `dotnet remove package` rather than editing XML by hand. Use shared version properties for related packages that must move together.
:::

## global.json

Pin the SDK so every machine and CI runner builds with the same version.

```json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "10.0.100",
    "rollForward": "latestFeature"
  }
}
```

## .editorconfig

The `.editorconfig` defines code style and naming rules, enforced by `dotnet format` in CI. The templates ship with a complete `.editorconfig` that covers:

- File-scoped namespaces, explicit accessibility modifiers
- `_camelCase` for private fields, `PascalCase` for types and constants, `I` prefix for interfaces
- Braces always, readonly fields, collection expressions, null propagation
- Analyzer severities (IDE0005, CA2007, CA1852, etc.)
- Relaxed rules for test projects (CA1707, CA2007, CS1591 off)

:::danger[Never modify .editorconfig to silence warnings]
The file defines the project's rules. Fix the code to match it. Changing a rule to make a warning disappear defeats the purpose of having one.
:::

## Local tools

Declare tools in `.config/dotnet-tools.json` so everyone (and CI) uses the same versions.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "isRoot": true,
  "tools": {
    "dotnet-stryker": { "version": "4.0.0", "commands": ["dotnet-stryker"] },
    "dotnet-reportgenerator-globaltool": { "version": "5.3.0", "commands": ["reportgenerator"] }
  }
}
```

Restore with `dotnet tool restore`. `dotnet format` ships with the SDK, so it needs no manifest entry.

---

## Solution Structure

A multi-project solution with strict domain isolation. Structure is enforced by architecture tests, not by convention alone.

The [dotnet.application](https://github.com/st0o0/dotnet.application) template ships with this layout. For libraries, the [dotnet.library](https://github.com/st0o0/dotnet.library) template uses a simpler structure without domain projects or persistence.

## Layout

```text
src/
  YourApp.slnx
  YourApp/                   # Host
  YourApp.Core/              # Common types, framework refs
  YourApp.Messages/          # Commands, queries, responses
  YourApp.Persistence/       # Versioned DTOs
  YourApp.Api/               # Internal REST API
  YourApp.Search/            # Domain
  YourApp.Download/          # Domain
  YourApp.Scoring/           # Domain
  YourApp.Search.Tests/
  YourApp.Download.Tests/
  YourApp.Architecture.Tests/
  YourApp.Tests.Shared/
```

## Projects

| Project | Responsibility |
|---------|----------------|
| Host | `Program.cs`, startup, DI composition, configuration |
| Core | Common types and framework references (Akka, etc.). References Messages and Persistence |
| Messages | Commands, queries, responses for all domains |
| Persistence | DTOs. Extend-only, versioned records |
| Domain projects | One per bounded context. No references to each other |
| API project(s) | Thin adapter layer that translates protocols to messages |
| Test projects | One per domain project, mirroring its folder structure |
| Architecture.Tests | ArchUnitNET structural rules |
| Tests.Shared | Shared test infrastructure |

## Reference direction

```text
Host -> API -> Domains -> Core -> Messages / Persistence
```

:::danger[Never upward, never cross-domain]
A project may only reference projects to its right. Domain projects never reference each other. They communicate only through messages defined in `Messages`.
:::


- **Core bundles framework references.** It declares the framework NuGet packages so domain projects reference only Core.
- **API projects are thin adapters.** They translate external protocols into domain commands and queries. No business logic.
- **Persistence DTOs are extend-only.** Add members, never rename or remove, so stored data stays readable.

## Domain isolation

Two domains that need to talk do it through a message contract:

```csharp
// YourApp.Messages
public sealed record QueryRuleSet(string RuleSetId);

// YourApp.Search sends it, YourApp.RuleSet handles it.
// Neither project references the other.
```

If two domains need the same type, it belongs in Messages (for contracts) or Core (for common utilities), not in one domain.

## Tests

- One test project per domain project: `YourApp.Search` is tested by `YourApp.Search.Tests`.
- Test folders mirror the source folders, so finding a test is mechanical.
- Shared fixtures and helpers live in `Tests.Shared`, referenced only by test projects.

## Architecture tests

Use ArchUnitNET to enforce the rules above so violations fail the build.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Domains_do_not_reference_each_other()
{
    var rule = Types().That().ResideInNamespace("YourApp.Search")
        .Should().NotDependOnAny(Types().That().ResideInNamespace("YourApp.Download"));

    rule.Check(Architecture);
}
```

Typical rules: reference direction, naming conventions, domain boundaries, and sealed-by-default types.

---

## Dev Environment

The application runs in Docker during development, together with the services it depends on. This keeps local behavior close to production.

The [dotnet.application](https://github.com/st0o0/dotnet.application) template ships with a `docker-compose.yml` and `Dockerfile` ready to use. Extend it with your service dependencies as shown below.

## Docker Compose

Use the compose file for local development, containing the app plus its dependencies.

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Development
      Download__MaxParallel: "2"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: postgres:17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev
    volumes:
      - dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  dbdata:
```

Start and rebuild:

```powershell
docker compose up -d --build
```

Stop:

```powershell
docker compose down
```

## Never `dotnet run` the app

:::danger
Do not start the application with `dotnet run`. Always use Docker Compose.
:::


Running outside the container diverges from the real environment: different paths, missing dependencies, different networking, and configuration that only exists in compose. Bugs found this way are often not reproducible.

This rule is about the *application*. Test projects are executables and are run with `dotnet run` as described in [Build Pipeline](../ci/build).

## Configuration

Pass settings as environment variables using the `Section__Key` convention. Compose is the single place where dev defaults for the container are defined. See [Options Pattern](../config/options-pattern) for how they bind.

## Frontend

If the solution has a frontend, keep it in its own project folder with its own package manager (pnpm or npm), and commit the lockfile.

```text
src/YourApp.UI/
  package.json
  pnpm-lock.yaml
```

```powershell
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Pick one package manager per repository and do not mix lockfiles.

## Hot reload

Where possible, use volume mounts so changes are picked up without a full image rebuild.

| What | Approach |
|------|----------|
| Frontend | Mount source and run the dev server (Vite HMR) in a container |
| Config files | Mount as a volume, restart the container |
| .NET code | Rebuild the image. `dotnet watch` inside a container is optional and only if it is reliable for your stack |

:::tip
Keep Dockerfile layers ordered so restore is cached (copy project files and `Directory.Packages.props` first, then source). Rebuilds then stay fast.
:::


## Checklist

- [x] `docker-compose.yml` runs the app and its dependencies
- [x] App is never started with `dotnet run`
- [x] Frontend uses a single package manager with a committed lockfile
- [x] Volume mounts for fast iteration where possible

---

# C# Conventions

---

## C# Coding Standards

Formatting and style rules enforced by tooling. If a rule is not machine-checked, it is still expected in review.

## Formatting

- Allman style braces: the opening brace goes on its own line.
- 4 spaces indentation, no tabs.
- Sort `using` directives with `System.*` first, then the rest alphabetically.

```csharp
using System.Text.Json;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

namespace Acme.Billing;

public sealed class InvoiceService
{
    public void Send(Invoice invoice)
    {
        if (invoice.IsEmpty)
        {
            return;
        }
    }
}
```

## Naming

| Member | Style | Example |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Public / protected members | `PascalCase` | `TotalAmount` |
| Private instance fields | `_camelCase` | `_clock` |
| `const` fields (any accessibility) | `PascalCase` | `MaxRetries` |
| Locals, parameters | `camelCase` | `invoiceId` |

```csharp
public sealed class RetryPolicy
{
    private const int MaxRetries = 3;
    private readonly TimeProvider _clock;

    public RetryPolicy(TimeProvider clock)
    {
        _clock = clock;
    }
}
```

## Language usage

- Use `var` when the type is apparent from the right-hand side.
- No `this.` qualifier unless it is necessary to disambiguate.
- Classes are `sealed` by default. Unseal only for a concrete need.
- Use `record` for messages, DTOs and value objects.
- Nullable reference types are enabled in every project.

```csharp
var items = new List<InvoiceLine>();      // type is apparent
IReadOnlyList<InvoiceLine> lines = items; // type is not apparent, state it
```

## Documentation

No XML docs. Names carry the meaning; if a member needs a comment to be understood, rename it.

:::tip
Use a comment only to explain *why* something non-obvious is done, never *what* it does.
:::


## Tooling

`dotnet format` is enforced and CI rejects violations. Run it after editing `.cs` files.

```powershell
dotnet format MySolution.slnx --verify-no-changes
```

:::caution[Never modify `.editorconfig` to silence warnings]
The `.editorconfig` defines the rules of the codebase. When it reports a naming or style violation, fix the code to match. Loosening the rule, lowering severity, or adding suppressions is not an acceptable fix.
:::


### Warnings as errors

`TreatWarningsAsErrors` is on for all projects, set once in `Directory.Build.props`:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

The build must stay at 0 warnings.

:::caution[Do not add `NoWarn`]
Fix the cause of the warning. `NoWarn` and `#pragma warning disable` hide real problems and accumulate as debt.
:::

---

## Type Design

Choose the type kind by what the type is for. The defaults below keep types small, safe to share, and cheap to reason about.

## Choosing a type kind

| Purpose | Type |
|---------|------|
| Messages, DTOs, API models, persistence events | `sealed record` |
| Small value objects passed around often | `readonly record struct` |
| Mutable state owned by one component | `sealed class` |
| Behavior with dependencies | `sealed class` |

## Records for data

```csharp
public sealed record InvoiceCreated(
    Guid InvoiceId,
    string Customer,
    IReadOnlyList<InvoiceLine> Lines);
```

Messages and DTOs carry immutable data. Use immutable or read-only collection types (`IReadOnlyList<T>`, `ImmutableArray<T>`) in their signatures.

## Value objects

Small, frequently passed values are `readonly record struct`. Equality and `with` come for free, and there is no heap allocation.

```csharp
public readonly record struct Money(decimal Amount, string Currency);

public readonly record struct CustomerId(Guid Value);
```

:::tip
Wrap primitive identifiers in a value object so `CustomerId` and `InvoiceId` cannot be swapped by accident.
:::


Use `readonly struct` (not `record struct`) when you need custom equality or no generated members. Keep structs small, ideally 16 bytes or less.

## Seal everything

Classes and records are `sealed` by default. Unseal only when you have a concrete, current need for a subclass.

```csharp
public sealed class PriceCalculator { }
public sealed record OrderPlaced(Guid OrderId);
```

Sealed types are faster to dispatch, cannot be extended in ways you did not design for, and make the intent explicit.

## Composition over inheritance

Do not build inheritance hierarchies for domain types. Compose behavior from small collaborators instead.

```csharp
// Avoid
public abstract class Document { }
public class Invoice : Document { }
public class CreditNote : Invoice { }

// Prefer
public sealed class Invoice
{
    private readonly ITaxPolicy _tax;
    private readonly INumbering _numbering;

    public Invoice(ITaxPolicy tax, INumbering numbering)
    {
        _tax = tax;
        _numbering = numbering;
    }
}
```

:::caution
A base class is a public contract with every future subclass. Prefer interfaces for polymorphism and records for data.
:::


## Mutable state classes

State owned by a single-threaded component (for example an actor, whose mailbox serializes access) uses mutable collections directly. No locking or immutable copies are needed.

```csharp
public sealed class OrderState
{
    private readonly Dictionary<Guid, OrderLine> _lines = [];
    private readonly HashSet<string> _tags = [];

    public void Apply(LineAdded evt)
    {
        _lines[evt.LineId] = new OrderLine(evt.Sku, evt.Quantity);
    }
}
```

:::caution
Mutable collections must never leave the owning component. Expose a snapshot as an immutable record instead.
:::


## No god classes

When a class has too many responsibilities, split by concern, not by size. Line count is a symptom; mixed reasons to change are the cause.

- One reason to change per class.
- Extract collaborators for distinct concerns (validation, mapping, persistence, orchestration).
- Do not create `Helper` or `Utils` classes as a dumping ground.

---

## Enum Conventions

:::caution[High-priority rules]
These rules are violated often and are costly to fix once values are stored or on the wire. Follow them exactly.
:::


## Every enum starts with `Unknown = 0`

`default(T)` must be detectably "unset". Every new enum declares an explicit `Unknown = 0` member.

```csharp
public enum DownloadState
{
    Unknown = 0,
    Queued = 1,
    Running = 2,
    Completed = 3
}
```

Unrecognized external values then bind to `Unknown` instead of failing model binding with an automatic 400. API handlers reject `Unknown` explicitly with the protocol's own error, before mapping.

## Persistence enums: explicit values on every member

Every member of every persistence enum has an explicit `int` value. The values are a stored contract.

```csharp
public enum PersistedDownloadState
{
    Unknown = 0,
    Queued = 1,
    Running = 2,
    Completed = 3,
    Failed = 5   // gaps are fine; 4 was never used or was removed
}
```

:::caution
Never change, reuse, or reorder stored values. New members get a new, unused value.
:::


## Enum-to-enum mapping: exhaustive `switch`

Map between enum types (API, message, persistence) with a `switch` expression that throws for everything unhandled, including `Unknown`.

```csharp
public static class DownloadStateMappingExtensions
{
    public static PersistedDownloadState ToPersistence(this DownloadState value) => value switch
    {
        DownloadState.Queued => PersistedDownloadState.Queued,
        DownloadState.Running => PersistedDownloadState.Running,
        DownloadState.Completed => PersistedDownloadState.Completed,
        _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(value), value, null)
    };

    public static PersistedDownloadState? ToPersistence(this DownloadState? value) =>
        value?.ToPersistence();
}
```

Nullable enums use null propagation at the call site: `x?.ToPersistence()`.

:::tip
Treat CS8509 (non-exhaustive switch) as an error, together with `TreatWarningsAsErrors`. Adding a member then breaks the build at every mapping that needs updating.
:::


## Anti-patterns

```csharp
// WRONG: numeric cast silently maps by position, breaks on any reorder
var persisted = (PersistedDownloadState)(int)state;

// WRONG: string conversion in a response record
return new DownloadResponse(State: state.ToString());

// WRONG: no Unknown member, default(T) looks like a valid value
public enum Mode { Fast = 0, Slow = 1 }

// WRONG: missing the throwing arm, unknown values map silently
state switch { DownloadState.Queued => PersistedDownloadState.Queued, _ => default };
```

:::caution[Never convert between enum types with numeric casts]
`(Target)(int)source` is forbidden everywhere. Always use a `switch` expression.
:::


## Serialization

- API enums serialize as integers. Do not register a global `JsonStringEnumConverter`.
- Use per-type string converters only where an external protocol requires string values.
- Query parameters bind directly to the enum type.
- Never put serialization attributes such as `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]` on message or persistence enums. Use them only on API enums where an external protocol requires it.

## Dates and times in responses

Keep rich types. Formatting is the serializer's job.

```csharp
// RIGHT
public sealed record ScheduleResponse(DateTimeOffset StartsAt, TimeOnly DailyAt, DownloadState State);

// WRONG
new ScheduleResponse(StartsAt: start.ToString("o"), DailyAt: at.ToString("HH:mm"), State: state.ToString());
```

`DateTimeOffset` stays `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeOnly` stays `TimeOnly`, and response records never call `.ToString()` on enum values.

---

## Async Patterns

Rules for asynchronous code, cancellation, time, and concurrency.

## No blocking on async

Never use `async void`, `.Result`, or `.Wait()`. They cause deadlocks and swallow or wrap exceptions.

```csharp
// WRONG
public async void OnMessage(Message m) { await HandleAsync(m); }
var result = client.GetAsync(url).Result;
task.Wait();

// RIGHT
public async Task OnMessageAsync(Message m, CancellationToken ct)
{
    await HandleAsync(m, ct);
}
var result = await client.GetAsync(url, ct);
```

:::caution
`async void` is acceptable only for UI event handlers, which this codebase does not have.
:::


## CancellationToken everywhere

Accept a `CancellationToken` in every async method and pass it down the entire call chain.

```csharp
public async Task<Invoice> LoadAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken ct)
{
    var row = await _db.Invoices.SingleAsync(i => i.Id == id, ct);
    return await _mapper.MapAsync(row, ct);
}
```

Tests pass `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` to every call that accepts a token (analyzer xUnit1051).

```csharp
[Fact]
public async Task Loads_invoice()
{
    var ct = TestContext.Current.CancellationToken;
    var invoice = await _service.LoadAsync(id, ct);
    Assert.Equal(id, invoice.Id);
}
```

## TimeProvider, not DateTime

Inject `TimeProvider`. Never read `DateTime.Now` or `DateTime.UtcNow` directly. This makes time-dependent logic deterministic in tests.

```csharp
public sealed class ExpiryChecker
{
    private readonly TimeProvider _clock;

    public ExpiryChecker(TimeProvider clock)
    {
        _clock = clock;
    }

    public bool IsExpired(DateTimeOffset expiresAt) => _clock.GetUtcNow() >= expiresAt;
}
```

In tests, use `FakeTimeProvider` and call `Advance(...)` instead of sleeping.

## No ContinueWith in actor code

`Task.ContinueWith()` bypasses the actor's threading guarantees and may run on any thread. Use `PipeTo` with explicit success and failure mappings instead.

```csharp
// WRONG
_client.FetchAsync(url).ContinueWith(t => new Fetched(t.Result));

// RIGHT
_client.FetchAsync(url, ct).PipeTo(
    Self,
    success: body => new Fetched(body),
    failure: ex => new FetchFailed(ex));
```

:::tip
Define your own `XxxFailed(Exception Cause)` message rather than relying on framework failure wrappers.
:::


## ConfigureAwait

Follow the project default. Do not sprinkle `ConfigureAwait(false)` on individual awaits.

- Application code (ASP.NET Core, workers, actors) has no synchronization context, so it has no effect.
- Libraries intended for general reuse may set it consistently, enforced by an analyzer, never ad hoc.

## Structured concurrency

Prefer higher-level primitives over manual `Task` management.

| Need | Use |
|------|-----|
| Producer/consumer, buffering, back-pressure | `System.Threading.Channels` |
| Stateful entities, serialized access | Actors |
| Parallel I/O with a bound | `Parallel.ForEachAsync` with `MaxDegreeOfParallelism` |

```csharp
var channel = Channel.CreateBounded<Job>(capacity: 100);

await foreach (var job in channel.Reader.ReadAllAsync(ct))
{
    await ProcessAsync(job, ct);
}
```

:::caution
Avoid fire-and-forget `Task.Run` and unobserved tasks. Every task must be awaited, piped, or owned by a component that observes its failure.
:::

---

# Akka.NET

---

## Actor Design Conventions

Actors are **thin plumbing**: message routing, persistence hooks and lifecycle. Domain logic and mutable domain state live elsewhere (see [State Management](state-management)).

## Naming

| Suffix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `*Manager` | Cluster Singleton |
| `*Worker` | Sharded entity or local entity region entity |
| `*Actor` | Everything else: pools, plain actors, children |

```csharp
public sealed class DownloadManager : ReceiveActor { }   // singleton
public sealed class DownloadWorker : ReceiveActor { }    // sharded entity
public sealed class ScoringActor : ReceiveActor { }      // pooled child
```

## Thin actors

An actor receives a message, delegates to its state object, and sends a reply. Nothing else.

```csharp
public sealed class CounterWorker : ReceiveActor
{
    private readonly CounterState _state = CounterState.Empty;

    public CounterWorker()
    {
        Receive<Increment>(cmd =>
        {
            _state.Apply(cmd);
            Sender.Tell(new IncrementCompleted(_state.Value));
        });
        Receive<QueryCounter>(_ => Sender.Tell(_state.GetSnapshot()));
    }
}
```

:::tip[Prefer one Receive block over many tiny handlers]
Keep actors simple. One constructor with a flat list of `Receive<T>` registrations
is easier to read than eight `HandleXyz` methods that each need a jump to understand.
Extract a method only when it is genuinely reused or hides real complexity.
:::


## Dependency injection and actor resolution

Use `resolver.Props<T>()` when an actor needs DI dependencies. Resolve other actors at runtime with `context.GetActor<T>()`.

```csharp
// Creating
var props = resolver.Props<ScoringActor>();

// Resolving a peer
var manager = Context.GetActor<DownloadManager>();
manager.Tell(new EnqueueDownload(id));
```

:::caution[Never pass `IActorRef` as a constructor parameter]
Actor refs injected through constructors are fixed at construction, break on restart
and hide the topology. Resolve through the registry or `Context` instead.
:::


## Async work: PipeTo, not ContinueWith

`Task.ContinueWith` bypasses Akka's threading guarantees. Use `PipeTo` with both `success:` and `failure:`.

```csharp
// Wrong
_client.FetchAsync(cmd.Url).ContinueWith(t => Self.Tell(t.Result));

// Right
_client.FetchAsync(cmd.Url, ct)
    .PipeTo(Self,
        success: r => new FetchCompleted(r),
        failure: ex => new FetchFailed(ex));
```

## Failures are project-owned messages

Never use Akka's `Status.Failure`. Define a failure record per operation.

```csharp
public sealed record FetchFailed(Exception Cause);
```

:::caution[No `Status.Failure`]
It is untyped, cannot be matched to the operation that failed and invites catch-all handlers.
Every `PipeTo` must supply a `failure:` projection to an `XxxFailed` record.
:::


## No EventStream

Do not use `EventStream.Publish` or `Subscribe`. Communication goes through explicit actor references (Tell/Ask via registry or `Context.GetActor<T>()`). Explicit wiring is traceable, testable with `TestProbe`, and does not leak messages between unrelated components.

## Checklist

- [ ] Name matches role (`Manager`, `Worker`, `Actor`)
- [ ] State in its own `<Actor>State.cs` class
- [ ] No `IActorRef` constructor parameters
- [ ] No `ContinueWith`, `Status.Failure`, `EventStream`
- [ ] Every `PipeTo` has `success:` and `failure:`

---

## Actor State Pattern

The "Pathfinder pattern": all mutable domain state lives in a dedicated state class. The actor only routes messages and calls `Apply`.

## Rules

1. State is a `sealed class` in its own `<Actor>State.cs` file. Not a record, not nested in the actor.
2. Mutable collections (`List<T>`, `Dictionary<K,V>`, `HashSet<T>`) are fine. Akka's single-threaded mailbox guarantees safe mutation.
3. Every public mutation method is named `Apply`, overloaded by parameter type. Never `ApplyFoo` / `ApplyBar`.
4. For primitives or multiple values, add a small wrapper record next to the state class and use `Apply(WrapperRecord)`.
5. `Empty` is a property, never a shared static field.
6. State is never sent to callers. Use `GetSnapshot()` to produce a response record and `FromSnapshot()` to reconstruct.
7. Persistent actors add `GetPersistenceState()` and `FromPersistence()`.
8. No domain fields on the actor (dictionaries, flags, counters). Infrastructure refs (actor refs, `CancellationTokenSource`, stopwatches) may stay on the actor.

## Correct

```csharp
public sealed class CartState
{
    private readonly Dictionary<Guid, int> _items = new();
    public bool CheckedOut { get; private set; }

    public static CartState Empty => new();

    public void Apply(ItemAdded evt) =>
        _items[evt.ProductId] = _items.GetValueOrDefault(evt.ProductId) + evt.Quantity;

    public void Apply(CheckedOut _) => CheckedOut = true;

    // wrapper record for multiple values
    public void Apply(QuantityChange change) => _items[change.ProductId] = change.Quantity;

    public CartSnapshot GetSnapshot() => new(_items.ToImmutableDictionary(), CheckedOut);

    public static CartState FromSnapshot(CartSnapshot s)
    {
        var state = new CartState { CheckedOut = s.CheckedOut };
        foreach (var (id, qty) in s.Items) state._items[id] = qty;
        return state;
    }
}

public sealed record QuantityChange(Guid ProductId, int Quantity);
```

## Persistent variant

```csharp
public PersistedCartState GetPersistenceState() => new(_items.ToDictionary(), CheckedOut);

public static CartState FromPersistence(PersistedCartState p)
{
    var state = new CartState { CheckedOut = p.CheckedOut };
    foreach (var (id, qty) in p.Items) state._items[id] = qty;
    return state;
}
```

See [Persistence](persistence) for how these hook into `Persist` and `SaveSnapshot`.

## Anti-patterns

:::caution[Leaked state on the actor]
```csharp
public sealed class CartActor : ReceiveActor
{
    private readonly Dictionary<Guid, int> _items = new(); // domain state on actor
    private bool _checkedOut;                              // flag on actor
    private int _retries;                                  // counter on actor
}
```
The actor now owns domain logic that cannot be unit-tested without an `ActorSystem`.
:::


:::caution[Misnamed or nested state]
```csharp
public sealed class CartActor
{
    private sealed record State(ImmutableList<Item> Items);   // nested record
}

public sealed class CartState
{
    public void ApplyItemAdded(ItemAdded e) { }   // not named Apply
    public void ApplyCheckedOut() { }
    public static readonly CartState Empty = new(); // shared mutable instance
}
```
A shared static `Empty` is a mutable instance reused across actors: one actor's mutation corrupts the next.
:::


:::caution[Sending state to callers]
```csharp
Receive<QueryCart>(_ => Sender.Tell(_state)); // caller now holds a mutable reference
```
Reply with `_state.GetSnapshot()` instead.
:::


:::tip[Why a class and not a record?]
The state mutates in place and is touched only from the actor's mailbox. Records with
`with` expressions allocate on every event and encourage leaking immutable-looking
copies that are never actually shared.
:::


## Testing benefit

State classes are plain objects. Test them directly without an actor system:

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Apply_ItemAdded_AccumulatesQuantity()
{
    var state = CartState.Empty;
    state.Apply(new ItemAdded(id, 2));
    state.Apply(new ItemAdded(id, 3));
    Assert.Equal(5, Assert.Single(state.GetSnapshot().Items).Value);
}
```

---

## Message Conventions

## Naming

| Kind | Name | Response |
|------|------|----------|
| Command | `VerbNoun` (`SearchSeries`, `AddDownload`) | `abstract record VerbNounResponse` with `VerbNounCompleted` / `VerbNounFailed` |
| Query | `QueryNoun` (`QueryRuleSetDetail`) | `abstract record NounResponse` with `NounResult` / `NounFailed` |
| Event (persistence) | Past tense (`ScoringRecorded`) | none |
| Config | Noun (`MatchingConfig`) | none, fire-and-forget |

## Command with responses

Command and its responses live in one file.

```csharp
// AddDownload.cs
public sealed record AddDownload(Guid DownloadId, Uri Source) : IWithDownloadId;

public abstract record AddDownloadResponse;
public sealed record AddDownloadCompleted(Guid DownloadId) : AddDownloadResponse;
public sealed record AddDownloadFailed(Exception Cause) : AddDownloadResponse;
```

## Query with responses

```csharp
// QueryRuleSetDetail.cs
public sealed record QueryRuleSetDetail(string RuleSetId) : IWithRuleSetId;

public abstract record RuleSetDetailResponse;
public sealed record RuleSetDetailResult(RuleSetDetail Detail) : RuleSetDetailResponse;
public sealed record RuleSetDetailFailed(Exception Cause) : RuleSetDetailResponse;
```

Callers switch exhaustively on the response:

```csharp
var response = await actor.Ask<AddDownloadResponse>(cmd, timeout, ct);
return response switch
{
    AddDownloadCompleted ok => Results.Ok(ok.DownloadId),
    AddDownloadFailed f     => Results.Problem(f.Cause.Message),
    _ => throw new InvalidOperationException()
};
```

:::caution[No domain-wide response interfaces]
Each command and query owns its response hierarchy. Do not introduce `IDownloadResponse`
or a shared `Result<T>` base across a domain. Shared response types couple unrelated
operations and make exhaustive matching meaningless.
:::


## Events and config

```csharp
// Persistence project, past tense
public sealed record ScoringRecorded(Guid ScoringId, int Score, DateTimeOffset At);

// Config: noun, fire-and-forget (Tell, no response)
public sealed record MatchingConfig(int MinimumScore, TimeSpan Timeout);
```

## Entity ID interfaces

Three layers, bottom-up:

| Interface | Member | Purpose |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| `IWithId` | `Guid Id` | Generic Guid identity |
| `IWithEntityId` | `string EntityId` | Routing key used by message extractors |
| `IWith*Id` | domain-typed property | The access point used in code |

Each `IWith*Id` inherits the lower layers and supplies default interface implementations. `Id` and `EntityId` are explicit implementations: invisible on the message, reachable only by cast, which only extractors do.

```csharp
public interface IWithDownloadId : IWithId, IWithEntityId
{
    Guid DownloadId { get; }
    Guid IWithId.Id => DownloadId;
    string IWithEntityId.EntityId => DownloadId.ToString();
}

public interface IWithRuleSetId : IWithEntityId
{
    string RuleSetId { get; }
    string IWithEntityId.EntityId => RuleSetId;
}

public sealed record InitDownload(Guid DownloadId, Uri Source) : IWithDownloadId;
```

### One `IWith*Id` per region

Each interface is a **routing address**, not a data type. Two regions with different purposes get separate interfaces even if the ID value is identical.

:::tip
`IWithRuleSetId` routes to `RuleSetWorker`. `IWithHistoryId` routes to `HistoryWorker`.
Both carry a ruleset ID string but are separate routing contracts.
:::


:::tip[Exception: domain-internal correlation]
Inside one domain, a single `IWith*Id` may span several regions when the ID correlates
one multi-actor flow (e.g. `IWithSearchId` across search and evaluation workers).
Sharing across domains is never allowed.
:::


## File organization

- One file per command or query, including its responses.
- Events and persisted state live in the persistence project (see [Persistence](persistence)).

---

## Persistence Conventions

Three tools, each with exactly one job.

| Tool | Job |
|------|-----|
| `Persist(evt, callback)` | Write the event to the journal. Stashes incoming commands until the callback runs. State update goes in the callback. |
| `DeferAsync(evt, callback)` | Run the callback **after all preceding Persist handlers complete**. Persists nothing; `evt` is not journaled or replayed. |
| `SaveSnapshot(state)` | Compact recovery for unbounded-growth actors. Interval-based. |

## Persist

```csharp
private void HandlePause(PauseCmd cmd)
{
    var evt = new PersistedPaused(cmd.Id, At: _time.GetUtcNow());
    Persist(evt, e =>
    {
        _state.Apply(e);
        Sender.Tell(new PauseCompleted());   // inline: single reply
    });
}
```

`Sender` is preserved inside `Persist` callbacks, so no `var sender = Sender` capture is needed (unlike `PersistAsync`).

## DeferAsync

Use when side effects are non-trivial **and** the handler does not call `Persist`/`PersistAll` itself:

- starting external processes or HTTP calls
- fan-out to two or more actors
- sending a response after nested Persists

```csharp
private const int SnapshotInterval = 10;

private void HandleCreate(CreateCmd cmd)
{
    Persist(new PersistedCreated(cmd.Id), e =>
    {
        _state.Apply(e);
        if (LastSequenceNr % SnapshotInterval == 0)
            SaveSnapshot(_state.GetPersistenceState());
    });
    DeferAsync("notify", _ =>
    {
        _manager.Tell(_state.GetRegistryUpdate());
        Sender.Tell(new CreateCompleted(_state.Id));
    });
}
```

:::caution[CRITICAL: never DeferAsync around a handler that persists]
If the handler calls `DispatchNext` or any method that calls `Persist`/`PersistAll`,
do **not** wrap it in `DeferAsync`. `PersistAll` inside `DeferAsync` breaks the event
batch pipeline: the inner events never reach the journal. Keep everything inline in
the outer Persist callback.
:::


Inline in the Persist callback is fine for a single `Sender.Tell`, logging, and metrics counters.

## Snapshots

- Only for unbounded-growth actors (singletons, long-lived entities). Short-lived entities with a handful of events need none.
- Interval-based: `LastSequenceNr % SnapshotInterval == 0`.
- Always snapshot the persistence DTO: `SaveSnapshot(_state.GetPersistenceState())`, never `SaveSnapshot(_state)`.

:::caution[Never snapshot unconditionally]
`SaveSnapshot` in every Persist callback doubles I/O per command.
:::


## PersistenceId

Singletons use a literal. Entities use a prefix plus the entity ID via the C# 14 `field` keyword: the getter adds the prefix, the constructor assigns the raw ID.

```csharp
// Singleton
public override string PersistenceId => "feed-crawl";

// Entity
public override string PersistenceId => $"download-{field}";
// constructor:
public DownloadWorker(string entityId) { PersistenceId = entityId; }
```

## Persistence DTOs

Live in a dedicated persistence project, separate from message types.

- **Extend-only records.** Add members; never remove or change existing ones.
- **No `Event`/`Dto` suffix:** `PersistedPaused`, `PersistedDownloadState`.
- **Explicit `int` values on every enum**, starting at 0. Never change, reuse or reorder.
- No serialization attributes on shared enums, no custom serializers.

```csharp
public enum PersistedSearchSource
{
    Unknown = 0,
    Api = 1,
    Manual = 2,
    Feed = 4      // gaps are fine; 3 stays retired
}
```

## Mapping

Conversion between domain messages and persistence DTOs lives in the **domain project** as `*MappingExtensions.cs`. The shared core references both sides but contains no mapping logic.

```csharp
public static class DownloadMappingExtensions
{
    public static PersistedDownloadStatus ToPersistence(this DownloadStatus s) => s switch
    {
        DownloadStatus.Queued => PersistedDownloadStatus.Queued,
        DownloadStatus.Done   => PersistedDownloadStatus.Done,
        _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(s), s, null)
    };
}
```

Enum conversion uses exhaustive `switch` expressions, never numeric casts.

---

## Akka.Streams Discipline

:::caution[Most frequently violated page]
These rules are the ones broken and corrected most often. Read them before writing any stream.
:::


## Rules

### 1. No context access in streams

Streams run on different threads than the actor's mailbox. Never touch actor fields, `Context`, `Sender`, or any mutable state from inside a stream lambda. Pass everything the stream needs as parameters when building the graph.

### 2. Flat pipelines

One flat `Source -> Flow -> Sink`. No streams inside streams, no nested `RunAsync` inside a stage.

### 3. No PipeTo inside streams

`PipeTo` belongs at the actor level, applied to the materialized result, not inside stages.

### 4. Use the built-in Ask stage

Use `.Ask<T>(actor, timeout)` rather than `SelectAsync(1, async x => await actor.Ask<T>(x))`. It handles parallelism, timeouts and failure propagation correctly.

### 5. No ContinueWith

Same as in actors: use `PipeTo` with `success:` and `failure:`.

### 6. No static helpers or custom GraphStages

Keep logic in the lambda. If it is too complex, it belongs in a service injected via DI, not a static helper or a hand-written stage.

### 7. No external state mutation

Side effects go into `DivertTo` / `WireTap` side channels, not into `Select`/`SelectAsync` lambdas that mutate outside variables.

### 8. Streams do not die in normal operation

If a stream terminates unexpectedly, find the root cause. Do not paper over it with restart logic.

## Correct pipeline

Everything the stream needs is passed in at build time. The actor only materializes and pipes the result.

```csharp
public sealed class HarvestActor : ReceiveActor
{
    public HarvestActor(IFeedSource source, IActorRef store, IMaterializer mat)
    {
        // Resolved on the mailbox thread, captured as plain values
        var storeRef = store;

        Receive<StartHarvest>(cmd =>
        {
            var done = source.Items(cmd.FeedUrl)                       // Source<RawItem>
                .Select(item => item.Normalize())                       // pure
                .DivertTo(
                    Sink.ForEach<RawItem>(_ => { }),                    // rejected -> side channel
                    item => item.IsRejected)
                .Ask<StoreResponse>(storeRef, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), parallelism: 4)
                .RunWith(Sink.Ignore<StoreResponse>(), mat);

            done.PipeTo(Self,
                success: () => new HarvestCompleted(cmd.FeedUrl),
                failure: ex => new HarvestFailed(ex));
        });
    }
}
```

## Hall of shame

:::caution[Context access inside a stage]
```csharp
.Select(x => { _counter++; Sender.Tell(x); return x; })   // actor fields + Sender
```
:::


:::caution[Stream in a stream]
```csharp
.SelectAsync(1, async x =>
    await Source.From(x.Children).RunWith(Sink.Seq<Child>(), mat))   // nested RunWith
```
:::


:::caution[Manual SelectAsync + Ask]
```csharp
.SelectAsync(1, async x => await store.Ask<StoreResponse>(x))
```
Use `.Ask<StoreResponse>(store, timeout)`.
:::


:::caution[PipeTo and ContinueWith in a stage]
```csharp
.SelectAsync(1, x => Save(x).ContinueWith(t => t.Result))
.Select(x => { Save(x).PipeTo(Self); return x; })
```
:::


:::caution[Static helper or custom stage]
```csharp
.Select(x => FeedHelpers.ParseAndMerge(x))     // static helper
.Via(new MyCustomGraphStage())                 // hand-rolled stage
```
Inject an `IItemParser` service and call it in the lambda.
:::


:::caution[Mutating outside state]
```csharp
var seen = new HashSet<string>();
.Select(x => { seen.Add(x.Id); return x; })    // shared mutable state across threads
```
Use `StatefulSelectMany`, `Sliding`, `GroupBy`, or a `WireTap` to a sink that owns the state.
:::


:::caution[Restart-on-failure as a fix]
```csharp
RestartSource.OnFailuresWithBackoff(() => flakySource, settings)   // hides the real bug
```
A source that dies repeatedly has a root cause. Fix it.
:::


## Review checklist

- [ ] Lambdas reference only parameters and injected services
- [ ] Single flat graph, one materialization
- [ ] `.Ask<T>()` stage, no manual `SelectAsync` + `Ask`
- [ ] `PipeTo` only on the materialized `Task`
- [ ] Side effects via `DivertTo` / `WireTap`
- [ ] No restart wrapper masking failures

---

## Cluster & Sharding

Three hosting shapes, each with a fixed naming convention.

| Shape | Suffix | Routing | Persistence |
|-------|--------|---------|-------------|
| Cluster Singleton | `*Manager` | one instance per cluster | literal `PersistenceId` |
| Shard Region | `*Worker` | entity ID via message extractor | `prefix-{entityId}` |
| Local Entity Region | `*Worker` | entity ID via `EntityIdExtractor`, node-local | `prefix-{entityId}` |

## Cluster Singletons

Use for coordinators that must exist exactly once: schedulers, registries, orchestrators. Name them `*Manager`. If persistent, use a literal PersistenceId.

```csharp
public sealed class DownloadManager : ReceivePersistentActor
{
    public override string PersistenceId => "download-manager";
}
```

## Shard Regions

Use for entities that must be distributed across nodes. Name them `*Worker`. Routing is based on the entity ID that messages expose through `IWithEntityId` (see [Messaging](messaging)).

```csharp
builder.WithShardRegion<DownloadWorker>(
    typeName: "download",
    entityPropsFactory: (_, _, resolver) => id => resolver.Props<DownloadWorker>(id),
    messageExtractor: new ShardMessageExtractor(),
    shardOptions: new ShardOptions
    {
        PassivateIdleEntityAfter = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)
    });
```

## Local Entity Regions

Same entity pattern as sharding (ID-based routing, passivation, message extractor) but local to the node. Use for request-scoped or short-lived entities that do not need cluster distribution. Entities self-passivate after finishing their work.

```csharp
builder.WithEntityRegion<SearchWorker, SearchKey>(...);   // EntityIdExtractor works with IWithEntityId
```

Because the protocol matches cluster sharding, an entity can migrate between the two without code changes.

## Passivation

:::caution[Choose the mechanism by region type]
- **Cluster sharding:** configure `ShardOptions { PassivateIdleEntityAfter = ... }` in the setup container.
  Never use `Context.SetReceiveTimeout` plus a manual `Passivate` inside a sharded entity.
- **Local entity regions:** the entity signals completion with a `Passivate` message to its parent.
  `EntityRegionOptions.PassivationTimeout` is only a safety net for stuck entities.
:::


```csharp
// Local region entity, done with its work
Receive<WorkFinished>(_ =>
{
    Sender.Tell(new WorkCompleted());
    Context.Parent.Tell(new Passivate(PoisonPill.Instance));
});
```

## Routing interfaces

- One `IWith*Id` per region. Each interface is a routing address, not a data type.
- Two regions with different purposes get separate interfaces even if the ID value is the same.
- Domain-internal exception: one `IWith*Id` may span several regions of the same domain when it correlates a single multi-actor flow.

:::caution[Cross-domain sharing is never allowed]
Domains talk through messages. A routing interface shared between domains couples them
at the type level and defeats domain isolation.
:::


## Choosing a shape

:::tip[Decision guide]
- Exactly one instance, coordinates others: **Manager (singleton)**
- Many independent entities, must survive node loss: **Worker in a shard region**
- Many short-lived entities tied to a single node's request: **Worker in a local entity region**
- Fixed-size parallel compute without identity: **`*Actor` in a pool** (not an entity region)
:::


## Singleton caveats

- A singleton is a potential bottleneck. Keep it thin and delegate work to workers.
- During handover the singleton restarts on another node, so state must be recoverable (persistence or re-derivable).
- Child actors of a singleton are created at runtime through `Context.GetActor<T>()` or `ResolveChildActor<T>()`, not via constructor-injected refs.

---

## Supervision Strategies

Supervision decides what happens when a child actor throws. Defaults are good; deviate deliberately.

## Default behavior

| Exception | Directive |
|-----------|-----------|
| `ActorInitializationException` | Stop |
| `ActorKilledException` | Stop |
| `DeathPactException` | Stop |
| Any other `Exception` | Restart |

For most actors this is correct. Do not add a strategy unless the default is wrong for your case.

## BackoffOnFailure for persistent actors

A persistent actor that fails during recovery or while writing will restart immediately and hammer the journal. Wrap it in a backoff supervisor so restarts are spaced out with jitter.

```csharp
var props = resolver.Props<DownloadManager>()
    .BackoffOnFailure(
        childName: "download-manager",
        minBackoff: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3),
        maxBackoff: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30),
        randomFactor: 0.2);
```

:::tip[Why backoff]
Journal outages are usually transient. Immediate restarts create a restart storm that
keeps the database overloaded. Exponential backoff with jitter lets it recover and
prevents many actors from retrying in lockstep.
:::


## Custom SupervisorStrategy

Override only when the default does not fit, for example a parent managing children that wrap flaky external resources.

```csharp
protected override SupervisorStrategy SupervisorStrategy() =>
    new OneForOneStrategy(
        maxNrOfRetries: 3,
        withinTimeRange: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1),
        decider: Decider.From(ex => ex switch
        {
            HttpRequestException => Directive.Restart,
            ArgumentException    => Directive.Stop,     // bad input will never succeed
            _                    => Directive.Escalate
        }));
```

- `OneForOneStrategy`: only the failing child is affected (the usual choice).
- `AllForOneStrategy`: all siblings restart together; use only when children share inseparable state.
- Always bound retries (`maxNrOfRetries` + `withinTimeRange`), otherwise a poison message loops forever.

## Escalation

`Directive.Escalate` hands the decision to the parent's supervisor. Use it for exceptions the current parent has no business handling.

```csharp
decider: Decider.From(ex => ex switch
{
    TransientIoException => Directive.Restart,
    _ => Directive.Escalate     // unknown: let the grandparent decide
});
```

:::tip[Escalation chain]
`Worker` fails with an unknown error, `Manager` escalates, the root guardian
restarts or stops the subtree. The further up it travels, the larger the blast radius,
so escalate only genuinely unexpected failures.
:::


## Never suppress errors

:::caution[Find the root cause]
- Do not catch and swallow exceptions inside `Receive` handlers to "keep the actor alive".
- Do not use `Directive.Resume` to ignore failures; it keeps corrupted state running.
- Do not wrap everything in a restart-forever policy to hide a bug.

A crash is information. Let it surface, log it with context, fix the cause.
:::


Prefer typed failure messages for expected failures, and exceptions for unexpected ones:

```csharp
// Expected, recoverable: model it
_client.FetchAsync(url, ct)
    .PipeTo(Self, success: r => new FetchCompleted(r), failure: ex => new FetchFailed(ex));

// Unexpected invariant violation: throw and let supervision handle it
Receive<Apply>(cmd => _state.Apply(cmd) /* throws on corrupt input */);
```

## Guidelines

- Persistent actors: BackoffOnFailure.
- Pools and routers: use the router's own strategy, rarely customized.
- Custom strategies: rare, documented with a comment explaining why the default fails.
- Escalate what you cannot handle; never swallow it.

---

# API Design

---

## Minimal API Endpoint Conventions

Endpoints are thin transport adapters. They translate HTTP into a message, ask a domain actor, and translate the response back into an `IResult`.

## File layout

- One static class per feature area, named `{Feature}ApiEndpoints.cs`.
- One extension method per class: `Map{Feature}Api(this WebApplication app)`.
- Constants (timeouts, `JsonSerializerOptions`) are `private static readonly` fields. They are the only non-lambda content in the class.

```csharp
public static class DownloadsApiEndpoints
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan AskTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);

    public static void MapDownloadsApi(this WebApplication app)
    {
        var group = app.MapGroup("/api/downloads");

        group.MapGet("/", async (IActorRegistry registry, CancellationToken ct) =>
        {
            var manager = await registry.GetAsync<DownloadManager>(ct);
            var response = await manager.Ask<QueryDownloadsResponse>(
                new QueryDownloads(), AskTimeout, ct);

            return response switch
            {
                DownloadsResult r => Results.Ok(r.ToApi()),
                DownloadsFailed f => Results.Problem(f.Cause.Message),
                _ => Results.StatusCode(StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError)
            };
        });
    }
}
```

## Handlers are inline lambdas

:::danger[No method group references]
Handlers must be inline lambdas. `private static` handler methods and method group references (`MapGet("/", HandleList)`) are prohibited.
:::


If a lambda grows too large, the logic does not belong in the endpoint. Move it into the domain layer (actor, service) and keep the lambda a one-liner per step.

## Lambda shape

Every handler follows the same three steps:

1. **Resolve** the actor from `IActorRegistry`.
2. **Ask** with a message. Use `request.ToMessage()` / `request.ToCommand()` when mapping is needed.
3. **Switch** on the response and return an `IResult`.

:::caution
No business logic and no multi-actor orchestration in the lambda body. If a request needs two actors, a domain-side coordinator owns that flow.
:::


The only non-inline code an endpoint may call is the mapping extensions, `IActorRegistry.GetAsync`, and `actor.Ask`.

## Route paths

| Rule | Example |
|------|---------|
| Groups use `/api/{feature}` | `/api/downloads` |
| Plural for collections | `downloads`, `rulesets` |
| Singular where natural | `system`, `setup`, `feed` |
| Sub-resources use consistent nesting | `/queue/...`, `/history/...` |
| Action on a resource | `POST /downloads/{id}/pause` |
| Collection-level action | `POST /downloads/pause` |

### Group root

The root of a group uses `"/"`, never `""`.

```csharp
group.MapGet("/", ...);     // correct
group.MapGet("", ...);      // wrong
```

## Exceptions

Self-contained health probes (setup checks) may live directly in the endpoint when no domain actor is involved.

## Checklist

- [x] One class per feature, one `Map{Feature}Api` method
- [x] Inline lambdas only
- [x] Resolve, Ask, switch
- [x] Exhaustive-style response switch with a failure arm
- [x] Root route is `"/"`

---

## API Models & Mapping

API models are a separate type world from domain messages. Mapping extensions are the explicit bridge between the two.

## Folder layout

```text
Models/
  Downloads/
    AddDownloadRequest.cs
    DownloadResponse.cs
    DownloadStatus.cs
  Feed/
  Shared/
    ErrorResponse.cs
    OperationResult.cs
Extensions/
  DownloadsMappingExtensions.cs
```

- Request and response records live in `Models/{Feature}/` subfolders.
- The namespace stays flat (`YourApp.Api.Models`). Subfolders are physical organization only.
- Shared types (`ErrorResponse`, `OperationResult`, shared enums) live in `Models/Shared/`.
- Enums live with the feature that owns them, not in a central `Enums.cs`.

:::note[One role per file]
A file contains either request records or response records, not both. The exception is a matched request/response pair for a single endpoint.
:::


## Enums over strings

Request and response records use enum types for every known finite value. Never use `string` for a value from a known set.

```csharp
public enum DownloadStatus
{
    Unknown = 0,
    Queued = 1,
    Running = 2,
    Completed = 3
}

public sealed record DownloadResponse(Guid Id, DownloadStatus Status, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
```

- Query parameters that represent enums bind directly as the enum type.
- Never call `.ToString()` on an enum in a response record.
- `DateTimeOffset` and `TimeOnly` stay typed. Do not format them as strings.
- Only exception: values passed through 1:1 to an external API.

:::tip[Unknown = 0]
Start every new enum with `Unknown = 0`. Unrecognized input binds to `Unknown` instead of failing with an automatic 400, and handlers reject it explicitly before mapping.
:::


## Mapping extensions

Mapping lives in `Extensions/{Feature}MappingExtensions.cs`.

| Method | Direction |
|--------|-----------|
| `ToApi()` | domain to API model |
| `ToMessage()` / `ToCommand()` | API request to domain message |

```csharp
public static class DownloadsMappingExtensions
{
    public static DownloadResponse ToApi(this DownloadSnapshot s) =>
        new(s.Id, s.Status.ToApi(), s.CreatedAt);

    public static DownloadStatus ToApi(this MessageDownloadStatus value) => value switch
    {
        MessageDownloadStatus.Queued => DownloadStatus.Queued,
        MessageDownloadStatus.Running => DownloadStatus.Running,
        MessageDownloadStatus.Completed => DownloadStatus.Completed,
        _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(value), value, null)
    };
}
```

### Enum mapping rules

- Use exhaustive `switch` expressions with a `_ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(...)` arm.
- Never convert between enum types with numeric casts (`(Target)(int)source`).
- Nullable enums: `x?.ToApi()`.
- A missing arm is a compile error when warnings are treated as errors.
- `Unknown` is handled by the `_ => throw` arm, so handlers must reject it earlier.

## Serialization

API enums serialize as integers. Do not add a global `JsonStringEnumConverter` and do not put serialization attributes on domain message or persistence enums.

---

# Testing

---

## Testing Philosophy

Tests exist to pin down behavior and catch regressions. They do not exist to
satisfy a coverage number. Every convention on the following pages follows from
this idea.

## Test behavior, not coverage

:::caution[A test that only checks "it didn't throw" is worse than no test]
It executes code, raises the coverage figure, and proves nothing. It gives
false confidence and makes later refactors look safe when they are not.
:::

```csharp
// Bad: executes the code, asserts nothing about the outcome
[Fact]
public void Score_DoesNotThrow()
{
    var ex = Record.Exception(() => _engine.Score(input));
    Assert.Null(ex);
}

// Good: pins the computed behavior
[Fact]
public void Score_TitleAndYearMatch_ReturnsFullScore()
{
    var result = _engine.Score(input);
    Assert.Equal(100, result.Value);
}
```

## Do not chase 100%

Spend effort where bugs actually hide.

| Test | Skip |
|------|------|
| Pure logic: scoring engines, parsers, validators, state machines | DI wiring and container registration |
| Mapping correctness (domain <-> DTO, enum switches) | Configuration binding |
| Edge cases in business rules (boundaries, empty input, ordering) | Trivial getters/setters and plain records |

## Tests fail for the right reason

When a test fails, the failure message alone should tell you what broke.

- One logical behavior per test, named after that behavior.
- Assert the exact expected value so the diff is meaningful.
- Prefer `Assert.Equal(expected, actual)` over `Assert.True(...)` (see [Assertions](assertions)).
- A test that can fail for several unrelated reasons is two tests.

## Mutation testing reveals weak tests

If a mutation tool can change `>` to `>=` and your suite stays green, the test
does not check what you think it checks. Use [mutation testing](mutation-testing)
on pure logic to find boundary conditions that no test pins down.

## One test class per production class

- `FooEngine` is tested by `FooEngineTests`, in the same relative folder.
- No shared base test classes with inherited tests. Inherited tests hide what is
  actually being run and make failures hard to trace.
- Small shared helpers (builders, fixtures) are fine; shared *test cases* are not.

## No `Thread.Sleep`

Never wait for async or eventually-consistent state with a fixed delay. It is
slow when the system is fast and flaky when it is slow.

:::tip[Use bounded waits with descriptive failures]
Use `AwaitAssert`, `TestProbe.ExpectMsg`, or an equivalent polling helper
with an explicit timeout. When it times out, the failure message must say
what was being waited for. Actor tests get this for free, see
[Actor Testing](actor-testing).
:::


## Quality bar

Reference point: a mature codebase of roughly 1200 tests across 11 test
projects, all passing, all meaningful. No test exists just because a metric
asked for one. If you cannot say what regression a test would catch, delete it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Does the test assert an observable outcome, not just absence of exceptions?
- [ ] Would a plausible bug in the production code make it fail?
- [ ] Is the failure message self-explanatory?
- [ ] Is there one test class per production class, with no inherited test cases?
- [ ] Are there zero `Thread.Sleep` or arbitrary delays?

---

## Assertion Conventions

Patterns for xUnit assertions. The goal is failures that point at the cause and
assertions that cannot pass vacuously.

## Collections

### Single element

Use `Assert.Single` instead of indexing. It asserts the count and binds the element.

```csharp
var item = Assert.Single(results);
Assert.Equal("Tatort", item.Title);
```

### Count guard before indexing

When several elements are accessed by index, assert the count first. Otherwise a
wrong count surfaces as an `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

```csharp
Assert.Equal(2, list.Count);
Assert.Equal("a", list[0].Name);
Assert.Equal("b", list[1].Name);
```

## Nullability

### No `!.` in tests

Do not use the null-forgiving operator to reach into nullable values. Assert
non-null first, then access members cleanly.

```csharp
var entry = result.Entry;
Assert.NotNull(entry);
Assert.Equal("x", entry.Name);
```

:::note[Exception]
XLinq `element.Attribute("x")!.Value` is accepted.
:::


### No vacuous assertions

Once a value is already proven non-null and of the right type (for example by
`ExpectMsg<T>()`), the next assertion must inspect actual content.
`Assert.NotNull` as a guard before property assertions is still fine.

```csharp
var msg = probe.ExpectMsg<DownloadCompleted>();
Assert.Equal(expectedId, msg.DownloadId);   // content, not another NotNull
```

## Values

:::caution["Not null" and "not empty" are almost never enough]
When behavior produces a concrete value (a string, a count, a computed
field), assert that exact value.
:::

```csharp
Assert.Equal("S01E02 - Pilot", name);        // good
Assert.False(string.IsNullOrEmpty(name));    // weak
```

Prefer `Assert.Equal(expected, actual)` over `Assert.True(actual == expected)`;
the failure message then shows both values.

## Exceptions

Capture the exception and inspect its fields, not only its type.

```csharp
var ex = Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(() => sut.Map(Kind.Unknown));
Assert.Equal("value", ex.ParamName);
Assert.Contains("Unknown", ex.Message);

var asyncEx = await Assert.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>(() => sut.RunAsync());
```

## Mocks

Specify exact arguments and call count (NSubstitute).

```csharp
files.Received(1).Delete(Arg.Is<string>(p => p.EndsWith("a.mkv")));
files.DidNotReceive().Delete(Arg.Is<string>(p => p.EndsWith("b.mkv")));
```

"Was called" or "did not throw" is not a verification.

## Types

Use `exactMatch: false` to prove interface or base-type conformance instead of an
unchecked cast.

```csharp
var handler = Assert.IsType<FooHandler>(obj);                   // exact type
var conforming = Assert.IsType<IFoo>(obj, exactMatch: false);   // interface/base
```

## Grouped assertions

Use `Assert.Multiple` for several assertions on the same object so one run
reports every failure.

```csharp
Assert.Multiple(
    () => Assert.Equal("Show", dto.Title),
    () => Assert.Equal(3, dto.Season),
    () => Assert.Equal(7, dto.Episode));
```

## Theories vs facts

| Use | When |
|-----|------|
| `[Theory]` + `[InlineData]` / `[MemberData]` | Small input/output sweeps with the same shape |
| Separate `[Fact]`s | Each case needs a large, distinct fixture (e.g. an embedded JSON payload) |

A readable failure name beats DRY when fixtures are large.

```csharp
[Theory]
[InlineData(0, false)]
[InlineData(1, true)]
[InlineData(100, true)]
public void IsValid_Boundaries(int value, bool expected)
    => Assert.Equal(expected, Validator.IsValid(value));
```

---

## Actor Testing

Conventions for testing Akka.NET actors. Examples assume xUnit.

## Choosing a TestKit

| Scenario | Use |
|----------|-----|
| Actor with DI dependencies, or resolved through the actor registry | `Akka.Hosting.TestKit` |
| Simple actor with no DI | Classic `Akka.TestKit.Xunit` |
| Pure state logic | No TestKit, see [State-only tests](#state-only-unit-tests) |

## Register TestProbes in DI

Actors resolve collaborators through the container or registry, so register
probes there instead of passing actor refs through constructors.

```csharp
public sealed class DownloadManagerTests : Akka.Hosting.TestKit.TestKit
{
    private readonly TestProbe _scheduler;

    public DownloadManagerTests() { _scheduler = CreateTestProbe("scheduler"); }

    protected override void ConfigureAkka(AkkaConfigurationBuilder builder, IServiceProvider provider)
    {
        builder.WithActors((system, registry) =>
        {
            registry.Register<DownloadScheduler>(_scheduler);
            var props = DependencyResolver.For(system).Props<DownloadManager>();
            registry.Register<DownloadManager>(system.ActorOf(props, "manager"));
        });
    }
}
```

## State-only unit tests

If actor state lives in its own class with `Apply(event)` methods, test that class
directly. No actor system, no timing, fast and deterministic.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Apply_Paused_SetsPausedFlag()
{
    var state = DownloadState.Empty;
    state.Apply(new Paused(Id));
    Assert.True(state.IsPaused);
}
```

Cover `GetSnapshot()` and persistence round-trips (`GetPersistenceState()` then
`FromPersistence()`) the same way.

## Interaction flows

For multi-step flows, chain `ExpectMsg` calls on probes. Each call is a bounded
wait and an assertion in one.

```csharp
manager.Tell(new AddDownload(id, url), TestActor);
var added = ExpectMsg<AddDownloadCompleted>();
Assert.Equal(id, added.DownloadId);

var dispatched = _scheduler.ExpectMsg<WorkAvailable>();
Assert.Equal(id, dispatched.DownloadId);
_scheduler.ExpectNoMsg(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200));
```

## Timeouts

:::caution[Never use `Thread.Sleep` or `Task.Delay` to wait for an actor]
Use `ExpectMsg`, `AwaitAssert`, or `ExpectNoMsg` with an explicit duration.
Timeouts belong on asynchronous operations only; they bound the wait, they
are not a way to "let things settle".
:::


```csharp
AwaitAssert(() => Assert.Equal(3, store.Count), duration: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
```

## Mocking rules

- **Plain interfaces** (`IDataFiles`, `IHttpClientFactory`, clocks, stores): use
  NSubstitute.
- **Actors**: never mock. Use `TestProbe` or the real actor.

```csharp
var files = Substitute.For<IDataFiles>();
files.Exists(Arg.Any<string>()).Returns(true);
// ...
files.Received(1).Exists(Arg.Is<string>(p => p.EndsWith("state.json")));
```

:::tip[Persistence]
Use the in-memory journal and snapshot store for persistent actors, and
recover by stopping and re-creating the actor with the same persistence id.
:::

---

## Mutation Testing with Stryker.NET

Mutation testing changes production code in small ways (`>` to `>=`, `+` to `-`,
a removed statement) and re-runs the tests. A mutant that survives means no test
noticed the change.

## Setup

Install Stryker.NET as a local tool so every developer and CI uses the same version.

```bash
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install dotnet-stryker
```

## What to target

| Good targets (deterministic) | Avoid |
|------------------------------|-------|
| Scoring engines, parsers, validators | Actor tests: timing-sensitive, flaky mutations |
| State classes (`Apply`) | Architecture tests: no production logic |
| Mapping extensions | Persistence DTOs: extend-only records |
| | Streams: timing-dependent |

## Configuration

One `stryker-config.json` per test project.

```json
{
  "stryker-config": {
    "project": "MyApp.Scoring.csproj",
    "test-projects": ["../MyApp.Scoring.Tests/MyApp.Scoring.Tests.csproj"],
    "thresholds": { "high": 80, "low": 65, "break": 65 },
    "ignore-mutations": ["string"],
    "reporters": ["html", "progress", "json"],
    "mutate": ["!**/Telemetry.cs"]
  }
}
```

- `break: 65` fails the run when the score drops below it. Start there and raise it gradually.
- The `string` mutator is ignored because log and wire text mutations are noise.

## Equivalent mutants

Some mutants cannot be killed because the behavior is identical (for example
`i < n` versus `i != n` in a loop that cannot overshoot).

:::caution[Do not weaken production code to kill a mutant]
Document equivalent mutants explicitly (a list next to the config, or a
`// Stryker disable once <mutator> : <reason>` comment) instead of
restructuring correct code.
:::


```csharp
// Stryker disable once Equality : loop bound is unreachable either way
for (var i = 0; i < items.Count; i++) { ... }
```

## Running

Locally, use a Docker container for a consistent environment:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src" -w /src/src/MyApp.Scoring.Tests \
  mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 \
  sh -c "dotnet tool restore && dotnet stryker -f stryker-config.json"
```

In CI, run the tool directly with `--local` where the job already has the SDK:

```bash
dotnet stryker -f stryker-config.json --local
```

## CI

Mutation runs are slow, so schedule them weekly and never on pull requests. Use
a matrix with one job per target project.

```yaml
name: mutation
on:
  schedule: [{ cron: "0 3 * * 0" }]
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  stryker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        project: [Scoring, Search, RuleSet]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with: { dotnet-version: 10.0.x }
      - run: dotnet tool restore
      - working-directory: src/MyApp.${{ matrix.project }}.Tests
        run: dotnet stryker -f stryker-config.json --local
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: stryker-${{ matrix.project }}
          path: src/MyApp.${{ matrix.project }}.Tests/StrykerOutput
```

:::tip[Workflow]
Read the HTML report, pick surviving mutants in boundary logic first, add a
test that pins the exact value, re-run. Treat the score as a signal, not a goal.
:::

---

## Architecture Tests with ArchUnitNET

Architecture tests turn structural conventions into failing builds. They live in
a dedicated project (for example `MyApp.Architecture.Tests`) and use
[ArchUnitNET](https://github.com/TNG/ArchUnitNET).

## What to enforce

- Reference direction
- Domain isolation
- Naming conventions
- One class per file

## Loading the architecture

```csharp
internal static class ArchitectureFixture
{
    public static readonly Architecture Architecture = new ArchLoader()
        .LoadAssemblies(
            typeof(MyApp.Core.CoreMarker).Assembly,
            typeof(MyApp.Search.SearchMarker).Assembly,
            typeof(MyApp.Download.DownloadMarker).Assembly)
        .Build();
}
```

## Reference direction

The allowed direction is `Host -> API -> Domains -> Core -> Messages/Persistence`.
Never upward.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Core_DoesNotDependOnDomains()
{
    var core = Types().That().ResideInNamespaceMatching(@"MyApp\.Core(\..*)?").As("Core");
    var domains = Types().That().ResideInNamespaceMatching(@"MyApp\.(Search|Download)(\..*)?");

    core.Should().NotDependOnAny(domains).Check(ArchitectureFixture.Architecture);
}
```

## Domain isolation

Domain projects must not reference each other. They communicate only through
messages.

```csharp
[Theory]
[InlineData("Search", "Download")]
[InlineData("Download", "Search")]
public void Domains_DoNotReferenceEachOther(string from, string to)
{
    Types().That().ResideInNamespaceMatching($@"MyApp\.{from}(\..*)?")
        .Should().NotDependOnAny(Types().That().ResideInNamespaceMatching($@"MyApp\.{to}(\..*)?"))
        .Check(ArchitectureFixture.Architecture);
}
```

## Naming conventions

| Kind | Rule |
|------|------|
| Actors | `*Manager` (singleton), `*Worker` (entity), `*Actor` (other); derive from an actor base |
| Messages | Commands `VerbNoun`, queries `QueryNoun`, events past tense |
| State | `<Actor>State`, sealed class |

```csharp
[Fact]
public void ManagerClasses_AreActors()
{
    Classes().That().HaveNameEndingWith("Manager")
        .Should().BeAssignableTo(typeof(ActorBase))
        .Check(ArchitectureFixture.Architecture);
}
```

## One class per file

ArchUnitNET inspects compiled types, so enforce this with a small file-based
test or an analyzer rule (for example IDE0065 / a Roslyn analyzer) rather than
the architecture model.

:::note[Allowed exceptions]
Small wrapper records next to their state class and a command with its
response records are deliberate groupings; whitelist them explicitly.
:::


## Do not over-constrain

:::caution
Keep the rules at the same level of detail as the reference project. Every
rule should encode a decision the team actually made and would defend.
Rules that block legitimate refactors, or that restate what the compiler
already enforces, create friction and get disabled.
:::


- Prefer a few rules on stable boundaries over many on incidental structure.
- Failure messages should name the rule (`.As("...")` / `Because("...")`).
- Never fix a violation by weakening the rule; fix the code or change the decision.

---

# DI & Configuration

---

## DI Conventions

Dependency injection is organized per domain and composed in `Program.cs`. The container is never queried by application code.

## Composable `Add*` extensions

Group related registrations into `Add*` extension methods on `IServiceCollection`. Tests can then reuse the same composition.

```csharp
public static class SearchServiceCollectionExtensions
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddSearch(this IServiceCollection services)
    {
        services.AddOptions<SearchOptions>()
            .BindConfiguration(SearchOptions.SectionName)
            .ValidateOnStart();
        services.AddSingleton<IValidateOptions<SearchOptions>, SearchOptionsValidator>();

        services.AddHttpClient<IMediaClient, MediaClient>();
        return services;
    }
}
```

## Per-domain setup containers

Each domain owns a setup container implementing a setup interface (for example `ISetup<IServiceCollection>`). The host applies them in a deliberate order.

```csharp
builder.Setups()
    .Add<LoggingSetupContainer>()
    .Add<TelemetrySetupContainer>()
    .Add<SearchSetupContainer>()
    .Add<DownloadSetupContainer>();

var app = builder.Build();

app.Setups()
    .Add<SearchEndpointsSetupContainer>()
    .Add<ApplicationSetupContainer>();
```

:::caution[Order matters]
Logging and telemetry are applied first. The application-level container is applied last, after every domain has registered its services and endpoints.
:::


Domain setup containers live in their own domain project. The host only references the container type, never the individual registrations.

## No service locator

:::danger
Never inject `IServiceProvider` to resolve dependencies on demand. Declare dependencies in the constructor.
:::


Legitimate exceptions are infrastructure factories that must create scoped instances (for example a hosted service creating a scope per unit of work, or an actor DI resolver). Keep them in one place and do not spread them into domain code.

## Options, not manual construction

- Never write `new MyOptions(...)` and register it as a singleton.
- Inject `IOptions<T>` (or `IOptionsMonitor<T>` / `IOptionsSnapshot<T>` when reload semantics are needed) everywhere.
- See [Options Pattern](options-pattern) for binding, validation, and `PostConfigure`.

## Validators live next to options

Register the `IValidateOptions<T>` implementation in the same `Add*` method that registers the options. A reader should find binding, validation, and start-up validation in one place.

```csharp
services.AddOptions<DownloadOptions>().BindConfiguration("Download").ValidateOnStart();
services.AddSingleton<IValidateOptions<DownloadOptions>, DownloadOptionsValidator>();
```

## Lifetimes

| Lifetime | Use for |
|----------|---------|
| Singleton | Stateless services, caches, HTTP client factories |
| Scoped | Per-request state (EF Core `DbContext`) |
| Transient | Lightweight, stateless helpers |

Never capture a scoped service in a singleton. Enable `ValidateScopes` and `ValidateOnBuild` in development to catch it early.

---

## Options Pattern

:::danger[Frequently corrected]
Do not build custom singleton resolution when `IOptions<T>` plus `PostConfigure` already exists. Reaching for a bespoke resolver, plan object, or info service is the most common mistake in this area.
:::


## The standard shape

```csharp
services.AddOptions<DownloadOptions>()
    .Bind(configuration.GetSection(DownloadOptions.SectionName))
    .ValidateOnStart();

services.AddSingleton<IValidateOptions<DownloadOptions>, DownloadOptionsValidator>();
```

- Use `AddOptions<T>().Bind(section).ValidateOnStart()`.
- Do not construct the options object manually and register it with `AddSingleton`.
- Consumers inject `IOptions<T>` (or `IOptionsMonitor<T>` when values may change at runtime).

## Computed and derived values: PostConfigure

When a value depends on other registrations or other options (for example, resolving requirements from the set of registered features), compute it in `PostConfigure`.

```csharp
services.AddOptions<PipelineOptions>()
    .Bind(configuration.GetSection("Pipeline"))
    .PostConfigure<IEnumerable<IFeature>>((options, features) =>
    {
        options.Requirements = features
            .SelectMany(f => f.Requirements)
            .Distinct()
            .ToArray();
    })
    .ValidateOnStart();
```

`PostConfigure` runs after all `Configure` / `Bind` calls, so it sees the final bound values and can safely derive from them.

:::note
`PostConfigure<TDep>` accepts injected dependencies, so there is no need for a hand-written factory or a lazily built singleton.
:::


## Validation: IValidateOptions

Use a dedicated `IValidateOptions<T>` class. Do not use inline lambdas in `.Validate(...)` for anything beyond a trivial one-liner.

```csharp
public sealed class DownloadOptionsValidator : IValidateOptions<DownloadOptions>
{
    public ValidateOptionsResult Validate(string? name, DownloadOptions options)
    {
        var failures = new List<string>();

        if (options.MaxParallel < 1)
        {
            failures.Add($"{nameof(options.MaxParallel)} must be at least 1.");
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.TargetDirectory))
        {
            failures.Add($"{nameof(options.TargetDirectory)} is required.");
        }

        return failures.Count == 0
            ? ValidateOptionsResult.Success
            : ValidateOptionsResult.Fail(failures);
    }
}
```

A class is testable in isolation, can take injected dependencies, and reports all failures at once.

## Defaults

Defaults belong in `appsettings.json` or environment variables, not in code.

| Do | Don't |
|----|-------|
| `"MaxParallel": 2` in `appsettings.json` | `public int MaxParallel { get; set; } = 2;` scattered across classes |
| Override with `Download__MaxParallel=4` | `options ??= new DownloadOptions { ... }` |

Required values should be `required` properties or validated, so a missing setting fails at startup instead of silently using a code default.

## Anti-patterns

- A `FetchPlan` / `ServiceInfo`-style object that recomputes state from several options. Use `PostConfigure` or a dedicated service that injects `IOptions<T>`.
- Custom singleton resolution or static accessors for options.
- `new MyOptions(...)` in application code.
- Validation that only runs on first use. Always call `ValidateOnStart()`.

## Decision guide
